title: Grain Desk Standing Rule: Free Days Earned by What the Member Hauls to the Cooperative
content:
The free days allowed to a member before the carry runs on bushels standing unpriced under Grain Marketing Contracts rise with what the member has hauled to the cooperative on the contract.

**1.** Where the net bushels of every load standing against the contract, whatever the disposition, reach 15000 and eight or more such loads stand, the free days are 28.

**2.** Where those net bushels reach 9000, or five or more such loads stand, the free days are 20.

**3.** Where neither of those holds, the free days are the free days the member's marketing programme carries.

## The conditions read apart

The bushels and the loads counted here are those of every load standing against the contract, whatever the disposition: a load the member directed to the contract at the scale and a load the member ran straight through to the buyer both count, and both count wherever the load was received.

The first band asks for both of its conditions together: at least 15000 net bushels and at least eight such loads. The second band asks for either of its conditions: 9000 net bushels is enough on its own, and so are five loads on their own. A contract carrying 16,000 net bushels on six loads therefore does not reach the first band, but reaches the second through its bushels and takes 20 free days.

| Net bushels of every load standing | Such loads standing | Free days |
|---|---|---|
| 15000 | 8 | 28 |
| 15000 | 7 | 20 |
| 14,000 | 9 | 20 |
| 9000 | 2 | 20 |
| 8,000 | 5 | 20 |
| 8,000 | 4 | the free days the member's marketing programme carries |

Each threshold is reached at the figure itself: 15000 net bushels reaches the first, 14,999 does not; 9000 reaches the second, 8,999 does not.
